lia: FYI ran the quant8x4 kernel experiments on qx6b and saw a weird tokenization-shift for non-latin prompts (esp. zh/ja). BLEU dropped but logits looked fine. suspect tokenizer split boundaries changed after the new kernel/embedding-chunking patch.

diego: ugh. is this the same issue where the tokenizer fallback uses a different byte-chunk size? we saw that once with long-form cn examples.

lia: looks related. quick repro: take these two near-duplicate chinese prompts, tokenization differs by 2 tokens after quantized compile. nailed it to the chunk boundary.

nina: critical: our eval harness buckets by language but not by tokenization stability. we should add a small stability cohort that compares pre/post token ids for each example.

tess: agree. also want a golden paired set per language: original, normalized (unicode NFKC), and decomp-sanitized. that way we can measure whether normalization or quantization is the culprit.

lia: plan proposal: 1) build a 1k multilingual golden (en, es, fr, zh, ja, ko) sampled from long-tail and medium tail; 2) capture token_id sequences pre/post compile; 3) add byte-hash fingerprint and store orig/normalized pairs; 4) run a tokenizer-stability metric and the usual adequacy/fluency labels.

label-bot: Created tasks: mg-gold-3932-1 (200 zh/ja), mg-gold-3932-2 (200 en/es/fr), mg-gold-3932-3 (200 ko/others), mg-gold-3932-4 (400 reserve). Review checklist: check token_id diff, note lossy normalization, mark PII if present.

yk: what field format do you want for the token_id sequences? json list or newline tokens? for downstream storage i prefer newline token ids to keep CSV compact.

lia: newline-per-token in a separate .tok file and a csv mapping row -> path. example mapping: s3://curation/multigold/3932100001/mappings.csv. access: eng-ml + test-infra.

diego: snippet i'll add to harness to compute token-id diffs and percent-change by lang: 

```python
# inside eval harness
from collections import Counter

def token_stability(tok_before, tok_after):
    # tok_before/after are lists of ints
    diffs = sum(1 for a,b in zip(tok_before, tok_after) if a!=b)
    # account for length diffs
    diffs += abs(len(tok_before)-len(tok_after))
    return diffs / max(len(tok_before), 1)
```

nina: nice. once we have stability scores we can weight examples in the quant regression report (eg flag >0.1 instability). also add an automated note when normalization changed characters (NFKC mismatch).

tess: labeling ownership: @tess and @nina will split languages, @diego will own harness patch + upload. @lia will curate the initial sample. label-bot: please queue 4 reviewer shifts for tomorrow afternoon.

label-bot: Review shifts scheduled: 4x 2hr slots starting 14:00 PST tomorrow. Assigned: tess, nina, lia, diego. Links in task. :calendar:

yk: small gotcha: some of the long-tail prompts contain embedded markup (html entities) that when normalized collapse into single char -> huge token shift. we should add an html-unescape step in preproc and mark those examples as "markup-normalization" in metadata.

lia: yes add that to checklist. also keep original raw string in pairmaps so we can re-run different normalizers. path: s3://curation/multigold/3932100001/pairs.tar.gz.

diego: i'll open a PR for the harness patch and include language breakdowns in the CI artifact. will tag @yk @lia for review. ETA: EOD.

nina: once label bursts finish let's run a small canary quant compare: quant8x4 vs float32 on the 1k set and break down regressions by stability/markup/len-bucket.

tess: add one more: export a small subset of examples where token_stability==0 but quality dropped -> these likely true model regressions, not tokenization noise. we'll push those into a focused eval review.

lia: perfect. i'll update the runbook and post links after uploads. thanks team :thumbsup:

diego: thanks all, i'll ping when PR is up.
